note: Ingrid, governance is not ready to show. The script defines the Trust Score properly, then twice speaks a figure of four point four that the platform no longer reports: the live product reads 3.8 out of 5, which also puts Supply Chain Health below the 0.85 target the same video says it must hold. verdicts.evidence: This is a live capture of the Supply Chain Health data product page. It shows a Qlik Trust Score of 3.8/5 (up 0.1), calculated for 1 dataset. The supply_chain_health gold dataset also scores 3.8/5. The description reads 'Generated by AI on October 23, 2026'. The page lists 1 API endpoint, shows the product activated in MCG Demo - Published, and names Robert Schoenfeld as owner.
verdicts.gap: The narration speaks the score twice, in sc2 and sc4, as 'four point four out of five'. This panel and the deck's own sc4 bullet and sc6 cards all show 3.8 / 5. At 3.8 / 5 the product is below the 0.85 target that sc6 says it 'has to hold'. Profiling (sc3) and the 'data quality behind the score' scene (sc6) show v3_dataquality.png. That panel is Qlik's stock semantic-type library, with every row created by Qlik on Jul 29 2025. It is not a profile of any MCG dataset, so the 8,200 / 640 / 2,400 figures exist only as drawn tiles. Lineage (sc5) is resolved by the platform but shows one hop, MCG Silver Transform to the product, cut off at the left edge. Bronze and the PostgreSQL source appear only as drawn HTML nodes. The stewardship sprint (sc7) cannot be read at render size. At full size it shows 0% progress, 0 assigned and 0 unassigned records, and its description says 'Salesforce contact addresses', although the CRM is the MySQL Meridian CRM. The glossary (sc8) shows every visible term in Draft with an empty Stewards column. The tenant records Robert Schoenfeld as owner of both products, but the sc6 cards show Henrik Jansen and Sophie Müller. Impact analysis (sc9) plays under the payoff line instead of the lineage line that describes it. It is also a 2026-09-24 capture with '1 change' still pending.

verdicts.evidence: Each has an owner with a name, a refresh schedule, a schema with semantic types, and a trust score target. Supply Chain Health has to hold zero point eight five.
verdicts.gap: The owner is never named aloud. 'a named owner' and 'an owner with a name' assert that a name exists without saying it, and Henrik Jansen appears only in small type on the sc6 card. The SLA is 'a refresh schedule' with no frequency; data_products.json says 15 minutes. The 0.85 target is spoken on a 0-1 scale while the score is spoken 'out of five', so a viewer cannot tell whether the product meets its target.

verdicts.evidence: The Qlik Trust Score — validity, completeness, discoverability and usage, in one figure. It does not live on a dashboard someone built. It is carried by the data product itself, computed by the platform and recalculated as the data changes.
verdicts.gap: The definition lands. However, the figure the narration then gives ('four point four out of five', followed by 'Nobody typed that into a wiki') is not the 3.8 / 5 the platform shows on screen. A viewer who reads the panel hears a typed-in number contradict the computed one, which undercuts the claim. This mismatch is scored under GOV-02.

verdicts.evidence: Eight thousand two hundred products with no weight on file. Six hundred and forty customer addresses we could not resolve to a location. Two thousand four hundred perishable items sitting in a warehouse with no lot number
verdicts.gap: All three counts are spoken and tied to the nightmares. Nothing on screen shows the tenant producing them: they are animated deck tiles over a panel that is not profiling output (see GOV-02).

verdicts.evidence: they land here, as a stewardship sprint. A steward who knows what a good Dutch address looks like fixes them, and the correction flows back into the pipeline automatically. Detection, notification, review, correction, validation. Automated at every step except the judgement.
verdicts.gap: The loop is told rather than seen closing. The sprint on screen holds no assigned or unassigned records at 0% progress, and the 'Correct: Talend job' step is a drawn node.

verdicts.evidence: A Data Quality Agent turns "every perishable item must have a lot number" into a rule and shows you the violations.
verdicts.gap: The governance video never mentions a Data Quality Agent; the line comes only in story four (s5_ai), so the cap applies. In s3 the 2,400 perishable positions with no lot number are never linked to a rule the agent wrote, and no violation list is shown.

verdicts.evidence: Every gold field traces back through its silver route, to the bronze landing table, to the source system. So when a number looks wrong, the question stops being "who do I ask?" and becomes "which node turned red?". It runs the other way too — change a source column, and impact analysis tells you exactly which products, apps and models you are about to break.
verdicts.gap: The narration is explicit about both lineage and impact analysis. The screen does not show the full chain it describes, and the impact view appears a scene later with one app and no model (see GOV-02).

verdicts.evidence: Twenty-five business terms, governed, in five categories. When someone says "on-time delivery", this is the definition, linked to the dataset that computes it.
verdicts.gap: 'Governed' is asserted but not defined: no term owner or steward is named, and no approval status is mentioned. The example, 'on-time delivery', is not one of the 25 terms in deploy/glossary_terms.json. On screen every visible term is Draft and the Stewards column is empty. The deck's five chips of five terms each match neither the source categories (Data & Technology, Governance & Compliance, Architecture among them) nor the source counts (6/5/5/4/5).

verdicts.evidence: which is the difference between a four-hour recall and an eleven-day one
verdicts.gap: EC 178/2002, Article 18's 'one step back, one step forward' rule, the NVWA, the lettuce recall and the citation that followed it are never named. A first-time viewer hears a recall-speed contrast with no regulator behind it. EC 178/2002 and NVWA appear only as small-print glossary rows in sc8.

verdicts.evidence: They are shareable over an API, and discoverable in the marketplace — so the next team does not rebuild any of this.
verdicts.gap: Landed. sc2 already makes the same 'shareable over an API … next team does not rebuild' point, so the script repeats itself. No consuming team is named, and no marketplace listing is shown: the product list is filtered to the Development space.
